screening.reason: Reports a diagnostic prediction (ASD vs. control) analysis of combined ABIDE I+II resting-state fMRI using 3D-CNNs on temporal summary measures, with both 5-fold and leave-site-out cross-validation (Inclusion 2, 3).

evidence_spans.text: We attained results competitive on this task for a combined ABIDE-I and II datasets of ~66%. When all summary measures were combined the result was still only as good as that of the best single measure which was regional homogeneity (ReHo).
evidence_spans.claim: The 3D-CNN achieved ~66% accuracy on the combined ABIDE I+II dataset; combining all summary measures performed no better than the best single measure (ReHo).

evidence_spans.text: The ABIDE I+II datasets is a collection of structural (T1w) and functional (rs-fMRI) brain images aggregated across 29 institutions (10), available for download2. It includes 1,028 participants with a diagnosis of autism, Asperger or pervasive developmental disorder-not otherwise speciﬁed (called ASD from now on), and 1,141 typically developing participants (CON).
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE I+II aggregates data from 29 institutions, with 1,028 ASD and 1,141 typically developing participants in the full release.

evidence_spans.text: We chose to cut off the minimum scan duration to 100-time points, which led us to include 96% of the whole ABIDE I+II dataset (N=2,085, N(ASD) =993), the vast majority of which (95%) with a minimum acquisition time of 4 min.
evidence_spans.claim: A minimum scan-duration cutoff of 100 time points retained 96% of ABIDE I+II (N=2,085, N(ASD)=993).

evidence_spans.text: The preprocessing was done using the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC, (12). We followed a preprocessing strategy adopted by the Preprocessed Connectome Project initiative3. This will allow others to replicate and extend the ﬁndings in this paper.
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing used C-PAC following a Preprocessed Connectomes Project strategy, chosen explicitly to enable replication.

evidence_spans.text: For the leave-site-out CV procedure, we selected ﬁve sites with the highest number of total subjects (ASD/total), namely New York University (NYU) (90/159), Kennedy Krieger Institute - 1 (KKI-I) (88/114), University of Miami - 1 (UM-I) (50/96), University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)-I (28/69), Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU)-I (42/64).
evidence_spans.claim: The leave-site-out evaluation used the five largest sites (NYU, KKI-I, UM-I, UCLA-I, OHSU-I) with each held out as the test set in turn.

evidence_spans.text: When assessed by ﬁve-fold CV procedure, all tested models performed at around 60% accuracy for the classiﬁcation task (Figure 2 and Table 2), with little variation between models' performances. On the contrary, the leave-site-out CV procedure shows high variability in terms of model performances with relatively good performance for the NYU site and poor performance for the other sites
evidence_spans.claim: Five-fold CV gave around 60% accuracy for all models with little variation, while leave-site-out CV showed high variability, good for NYU and poor for other sites.

evidence_spans.text: The overall best performing model was the MM-ensemble, which achieved balanced accuracy of 64% and F1 score of 66%, averaged over the ﬁve-folds of the CV procedure. With the leave- site-out CV procedure the performance of the MM-ensemble dropped to an average balanced accuracy of mean 56% and F1 score of 59%, suggesting that this model does not do well in generalizing to new sites.
evidence_spans.claim: The best model (MM-ensemble) reached 64% balanced accuracy / 66% F1 under 5-fold CV, dropping to 56% balanced accuracy / 59% F1 under leave-site-out CV.

evidence_spans.text: The code used of all the experiments performed is available on GitHub1.
evidence_spans.claim: All experiment code is publicly released on GitHub.

assessments.support: Full-release composition and the exact inclusion rule (>=100 time points, yielding N=2,085, N(ASD)=993) are explicit: "We chose to cut off the minimum scan duration to 100-time points, which led us to include 96% of the whole ABIDE I+II dataset (N=2,085, N(ASD) =993), the vast majority of which (95%) with a minimum acquisition time of 4 min."

Pipeline (C-PAC, following a published Preprocessed Connectomes Project strategy chosen explicitly for replicability) is specified: "The preprocessing was done using the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC, (12). We followed a preprocessing strategy adopted by the Preprocessed Connectome Project initiative3. This will allow others to replicate and extend the ﬁndings in this paper."
Diagnosis source is not described in this paper beyond citing the ABIDE release and its diagnostic categories (autism, Asperger, PDD-NOS).

Both 5-fold CV (with a validation split separate from the test fold) and an independent leave-site-out CV across the five largest sites are reported, directly exposing the gap between pooled and cross-site generalisation: "The overall best performing model was the MM-ensemble, which achieved balanced accuracy of 64% and F1 score of 66%, averaged over the ﬁve-folds of the CV procedure. With the leave- site-out CV procedure the performance of the MM-ensemble dropped to an average balanced accuracy of mean 56% and F1 score of 59%, suggesting that this model does not do well in generalizing to new sites."

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort composition, the inclusion rule, pipeline and both pooled (5-fold) and leave-site-out cross-validation are all explicitly reported, with code openly released; the only unreported item is the diagnostic label source.

charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes), following a Preprocessed Connectomes Project preprocessing strategy
charting.specific_features: Voxel-wise temporal summary measures (regional homogeneity, ALFF, fALFF, degree centrality, eigenvector centrality, local functional connectivity density, entropy, voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity, autocorrelation lag), each used as a full 3D volume input to a 3D-CNN
charting.model_category: 3D convolutional neural network (per-measure and multi-measure ensemble/combined models); linear SVM baseline
charting.specific_algorithms: 3D-CNN on each single summary measure (SM-model); MM-ensemble (majority vote across SM-models); MM-model (concatenated summary measures); linear SVM equivalents of each
charting.validation_methodology: Five-fold cross-validation (with an inner training/validation split) and a separate leave-site-out cross-validation across the five largest sites (NYU, KKI-I, UM-I, UCLA-I, OHSU-I), each held out as test site in turn
charting.key_performance_results: 5-fold CV: best model (MM-ensemble, 3D-CNN) balanced accuracy 64% / F1 66%; ReHo single-measure model comparable. Leave-site-out CV: MM-ensemble dropped to 56% balanced accuracy / 59% F1, with good performance for NYU and poor performance for other sites, indicating limited cross-site generalisation. Linear-SVM gave comparable results (~60% accuracy; MM-ensemble 66%/67%).
charting.dataset_openly_available: Yes — all experiment code is released publicly on GitHub.

domain_2_predictors_preprocessing.support: Pipeline is clearly named and justified for replicability, but no atlas is used (voxel-wise analysis) and no pipeline version is given (CL3, CL4).

domain_3_outcome_label_source.support: Diagnostic label source is not described beyond citing the ABIDE diagnostic categories.

domain_4_bias_transparency.support: Both pooled and leave-site-out CV are reported with contamination-avoiding validation splits, code is openly released on GitHub (CL5-CL7).

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (3D-CNN on voxel-wise rs-fMRI summary measures) using combined ABIDE I+II (N=2,085 after a minimum scan-duration QC cutoff; 993 ASD, 1,092 TD; 29 institutions).
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed voxel-wise temporal summary measures (ReHo, ALFF, fALFF, degree/eigenvector centrality, LFCD, entropy, VMHC, autocorrelation lag) fed into per-measure and ensemble/combined 3D-CNN models and linear-SVM equivalents; evaluated via five-fold CV and a separate leave-site-out CV across the five largest sites.
narrative_row.outcomes: Best model (MM-ensemble) reached 64% balanced accuracy/66% F1 under five-fold CV, comparable to the single ReHo measure, but dropped to 56% balanced accuracy/59% F1 under leave-site-out CV, generalising well only to the NYU site.
narrative_row.key_limitations: No motion/FD-based QC threshold reported (only a scan-duration cutoff); no atlas/ROI parcellation used; diagnostic label source not described; large drop in performance under leave-site-out evaluation indicates limited cross-site generalisation.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A methodologically strong example directly quantifying the gap between pooled cross-validation and leave-site-out generalisation on combined ABIDE I+II, with openly released code, highly relevant to assessing site-generalisation claims in ABIDE-based prediction studies.

kg_link.cohort_description: Full ABIDE I+II release (1,028 ASD/1,141 TD, 29 institutions) filtered by a minimum scan-duration cutoff (>=100 time points), retaining 96% of the release: N=2,085 (993 ASD).
kg_link.sites: 29 institutions overall; leave-site-out evaluation used the 5 largest (NYU, KKI-I, UM-I, UCLA-I, OHSU-I)
kg_link.pipeline: C-PAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes), following a Preprocessed Connectomes Project strategy
kg_link.atlas: None — voxel-wise whole-brain summary-measure volumes (no ROI parcellation)
kg_link.finding: Best model (3D-CNN MM-ensemble) achieved 64% balanced accuracy/66% F1 under five-fold CV, dropping to 56% balanced accuracy/59% F1 under leave-site-out CV across the five largest ABIDE sites, showing substantially weaker cross-site generalisation than pooled CV suggests.
evidence_quotes: We chose to cut off the minimum scan duration to 100-time points, which led us to include 96% of the whole ABIDE I+II dataset (N=2,085, N(ASD) =993), the vast majority of which (95%) with a minimum acquisition time of 4 min.

For the leave-site-out CV procedure, we selected ﬁve sites with the highest number of total subjects (ASD/total), namely New York University (NYU) (90/159), Kennedy Krieger Institute - 1 (KKI-I) (88/114), University of Miami - 1 (UM-I) (50/96), University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)-I (28/69), Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU)-I (42/64).

The overall best performing model was the MM-ensemble, which achieved balanced accuracy of 64% and F1 score of 66%, averaged over the ﬁve-folds of the CV procedure. With the leave- site-out CV procedure the performance of the MM-ensemble dropped to an average balanced accuracy of mean 56% and F1 score of 59%, suggesting that this model does not do well in generalizing to new sites.
